key_insight: A simple retargeting-to-RL recipe, proven in humanoid control, can be adapted to dexterous manipulation to learn contact-rich skills more efficiently. The paper’s key takeaway is that minimalist motion guidance can still help policies discover precise, force-aware hand behaviors.
problem_solved: Dexterous manipulation is hard because it requires stable contact handling, fine force regulation, and switching between complex contact modes. The paper asks whether a lightweight retargeting-guided RL pipeline can make these skills easier to learn without heavy task-specific engineering.
method: Retarget human or demonstration motions into robot-friendly kinematic references for manipulation.
Train reinforcement learning policies to track these references while handling contact-rich interactions.
Use a minimalist pipeline (REGRIND) that relies on simple guidance rather than extensive hand-designed rewards or controllers.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that dexterous manipulation may be more approachable with a clean retargeting + RL setup instead of highly specialized control stacks. It points toward more scalable skill learning for robot hands and practical transfer from human motion to robotic manipulation.

paper_title: A Minimalist Retargeting-Guided Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Dexterous Manipulation
paper_authors: Yunhai Feng, Natalie Leung, Jiaxuan Wang, Lujie Yang, Haozhi Qi
